---
title: "Revenue from a 0.5% City of Albany add-on sales tax"
toc: false
number-sections: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
source(here("R", "04_allocate.R"))
ALB <- list("Albany city, New York", "3601000", "36001", "ALBANY", "ALBANY")
appo <- do.call(apportion_city, ALB)
fit  <- fit_calibration(build_calibration())
est  <- apply_calibration(fit, sum(appo$B_cg, na.rm = TRUE))
phi  <- mean(albany_phi()$phi)
rev  <- function(b) 0.005 * b * (1 - phi) / 1e6
```

A reproducible estimate of what the City of Albany, New York would raise from a
0.5 percentage-point sales and use tax layered on the existing 8% — on the same
base Albany County taxes at 4%, with no preemption and no change to county
distributions.

::: {.callout-note}
## Headline
**About \$`r sprintf("%.1f", rev(est$B_c_central))` million a year**, with a
68% range of \$`r sprintf("%.1f", rev(est$lo68))`–`r sprintf("%.1f", rev(est$hi68))` million
and a 90% range of \$`r sprintf("%.1f", rev(est$lo90))`–`r sprintf("%.1f", rev(est$hi90))` million,
at 2022–2025 activity levels. A reasonable planning range is \$10–15 million.
:::

## Reproducing it

Source, cached data pulls with SHA-256 provenance, and the verified schema notes
for every dataset are in the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/donboyd5/albany_sales_tax). Clone,
`renv::restore()`, add a Census API key to `.Renviron`, and `quarto render`.
